question: Should OpenClaw accept static `sandbox.docker.env` SecretRefs when the resolved values still become Docker environment variables visible through Docker/container metadata?
rationale: The code change is bounded and additive, but the durable product/security boundary is whether SecretRef-backed credentials should be allowed on a Docker env surface that Docker operators and sandboxed processes can inspect.

options.title: Accept with explicit boundary
options.body: Land the linked PR only after a maintainer/security reviewer records that this exposure is acceptable with aligned docs, audit, plan, and configure behavior.

options.title: Require stronger docs first
options.body: Ask the linked PR to explicitly name SecretRef-backed Docker env exposure before landing the implementation.

options.title: Reject env delivery
options.body: Pause this direction and design a non-env secret delivery mechanism if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable.

recommendation.title: Accept with explicit boundary
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR only after a maintainer/security reviewer records that this exposure is acceptable with aligned docs, audit, plan, and configure behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has the strongest recent merged history across both Docker env propagation and SecretRef runtime resolution for this boundary.
